segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, it didn't move the needle much for me ... it just didn't carry the same weight as the geolocation.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant discounts the unfavorable family-residence report because it does not fit the go decision built around the SIGINT hit, without a specific evidentiary reason.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Really it came down to launch or delay twenty-four hours ... the surveillance option didn't get serious airtime.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The response narrows the course-of-action set to launch or delay and treats an available surveillance-only option as outside the real repertoire because the troop defaults to assaulting the tasking.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The firefight sticks with you ... when I pictured that wadi, I pictured tracer fire, not a calm crossing, even though nothing in the current threat picture pointed to that.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A vivid personal firefight memory disproportionately shapes current route-risk assessment over the current threat picture.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: At the same time, we'd had three clean runs through there recently ... I went with the wadi route mostly on that combination rather than waiting on updated route-specific intel.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats the recent run of quiet crossings as relevant to whether contact will continue or is due, rather than evaluating the current crossing independently.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Not specifically for the route. Time was a factor — we were already tight against the assault window.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a separate decision not to request route-specific clarification; the stated time constraint is a plausible non-bias explanation and is not itself a hidden target instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Rear wall we'd rehearsed extensively in training ... it felt less likely to go wrong than the front gate, even though I didn't actually have a current read showing the rear wall was any safer.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Ease of mentally simulating the rehearsed rear-wall sequence is treated as evidence of lower failure risk despite comparative structural and activity information favoring consideration of the gate.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I went with Team 1's call ... they're my organic element ... the front gate never really competed for my attention.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant favors the organic team's report over the host-nation report at the same location based on affiliation and built-in trust, in addition to the report-specific difference in vagueness.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We'd used that exact exfil sequence successfully the last two times ... both of those added complexity or delay I didn't think we needed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Prior success and avoiding added complexity are stated as the initial rationale, but this span alone does not explicitly show failure to adjust for the current casualty and ISR gap; the hidden mechanism is localized to the subsequent reweighting reflection.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Not as much as maybe they should have, looking back ... I don't think I fully re-weighted for the fact that this time we had a man down and less coverage than we'd had before.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly acknowledges projecting confidence from two prior successes without sufficiently adjusting for worse current conditions, which is the hidden optimism mechanism.
